props.gloss_en: the mishna: fat [of offerings] is subject to me'ila
R' Yannai: the verse says 'as it is taken off from the ox of the peace offering' (Lev 4:10) -- it juxtaposes the peace-offering ox to the anointed priest's bull
Rabbi: 'all the fat is the Lord's' (Lev 3:16) -- to include the sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity for me'ila
Abaye: had the Merciful One written [only] 'fat', I would say fat yes, the diaphragm and the two kidneys no; so the Merciful One wrote 'as it is taken off'
Abaye: had the Merciful One written [only] 'as it is taken off', I would say the fat of the tail, which is not in an ox, no; so the Merciful One wrote 'all fat'
Rav Zevid: 'all fat of ox, sheep and goat' (Lev 7:23) -- [the eating ban covers only] a thing equal in ox, sheep and goat
Rav Ashi: it is called 'its fat, the tail'; it is not called 'fat' plainly
